overview: SwitchAura is an empty placeholder. The entire file is the class declaration with no body members: no Module base class, no settings, no event handler, no packet code. It is not registered in ModuleManager, not referenced by Aura.java (whose mode dispatcher wires "Single", "Multi" and "Hypixel" to SingleAura, MultiAura and HypixelAura), and not instantiated anywhere in the source tree. The class has zero runtime effect: it cannot be toggled, emits no packets, and changes no client state. The name suggests a switch-style aura variant (target or weapon switching); the live sibling classes in the same package define the technique family it was presumably meant to join.

sections.p: The class body is empty: no extends Module, no constructor, no fields, no methods. Contrast with the live siblings: SingleAura, MultiAura and HypixelAura are static helper classes with a doUpdate method, and Aura.java dispatches to them from its UpdateEvent handler based on the registered modes. A grep for SwitchAura across the client finds only the class file itself; ModuleManager and Aura.java never mention it. The file is orphaned source, most likely the skeleton of a planned aura mode (target switching between multiple players, or weapon switching via C09 before the attack) that was never implemented or never wired into the dispatcher.

SingleAura shows what a switch aura would have looked like: CombatUtil.getTarget picks a target within range, RotationUtils.getRotations computes the aim, the yaw and pitch are written into the UpdateEvent so the C03 look follows, and the send path is swingItem plus C02PacketUseEntity ATTACK with a C08 autoblock at a fake BlockPos(-0.2223, -0.132, -0.312) and a C07 release, all gated by a Timer.delay(1000 / clickSpeed) cadence that resets on fire. A weapon-switching variant would add the C09 held-slot swap around the attack; none of that exists in SwitchAura.

There is nothing on the wire and nothing to detect. The class never registers with the event bus, never sends a packet, and never touches client state, so it is invisible to every anticheat by construction, not by evasion. The honest countering story is therefore the set of checks a real switch-aura implementation would face, each stated as a boundary: the checks fire on the C02 attack and C09 slot-switch stream the stub never produces.

files.label: SwitchAura.java (empty stub)
files.explanation: The file is four lines: the package declaration, the class declaration and a closing brace. It does not extend Module, has no constructor, no fields and no handlers, so it is not a module at all in the client's registration sense: ModuleManager never lists it and Aura.java's dispatcher has no matching mode. The analysis treats the stub itself as the finding, with the live siblings defining the technique family it never joined.

files.label: SingleAura.java (live sibling)
files.explanation: SingleAura is the closest live implementation of the aura family and the reference for what SwitchAura was meant to be. Its static doUpdate picks a target via CombatUtil.getTarget, writes RotationUtils rotations into the UpdateEvent, sends C02 ATTACK with swingItem, maintains an autoblock latch with C08 at a fake BlockPos and C07 release, and gates the cadence with a Timer.delay(1000 / clickSpeed) that resets after each release. Any real switch-aura variant would share this packet footprint, which is what the countering entries describe.

countering.label: Hawk ItemSwitchSpeed (same-tick switch and use)
countering.explanation: ItemSwitchSpeed records every interact (attack, use, place) into a usedSomething set and, on the next C09 item switch, punishes when the switch lands fewer than minSwitchTicks (default 1) after the previous switch. A weapon-switch aura that swaps to the best sword and attacks within the same tick presents a zero-gap C09 followed by the C02, so the check punishes every cycle, and being Cancelless it accumulates VL without a cancel. The stub sends neither packet, so the check never fires; the entry defines the detection surface of the technique the stub names.

countering.label: NCP fight Reach (attack distance)
countering.explanation: A live switch aura attacks with the C02 half of its stream, and NCP fight Reach measures that attack from the server-tracked position against the 4.02 survival distance limit (DefaultConfig line 366) with a reachMod reduce band from 3.22 to 4.02 that silently cancels repeat hits. The sibling auras aim and attack inside a 6 to 8 block range, so a stock-range switch aura stays inside the limit and the check is a boundary for over-extended configurations rather than a guaranteed catch. For the stub the check is purely hypothetical: no C02 ever exists.

countering.label: NCP fight Angle (rotation stream)
countering.explanation: The sibling auras write instantaneous RotationUtils aims into the UpdateEvent, so a live switch aura produces the classic aura rotation stream: fixed convergence on the target, near-zero yaw variance between attacks, and sharp target switches when the nearest-target order changes. NCP fight Angle scores those signals in a 1000ms window with 0.98 decay, and it is config-gated: dormant at the stock thresholds (move 100, time 150, yaw 60, switch 50) and flagging on detection configs. The empty stub produces no rotation at all, so the check is an honest boundary describing the companion stream, not a detector of the class.

countering.label: Arc v2 KillAura (multi-signal combat check)
countering.explanation: Arc v2 KillAura combines maxAngle, maxSwingTime and maxReach signals on the C02 stream, catching the signature of an aura: attacks whose facing misses the target's direction cone, swings at rates a human cannot sustain, and hits beyond the reach bound. A live switch aura using the sibling's instant RotationUtils aim would trip the angle component when the snap exceeds the configured maxAngle. The stub sends no C02, no C09 and no swing, so none of the three signals ever exist; the entry is the honest statement of what a real implementation would face.
